podcast.title: Death
podcast.body: Edward Hill died of a stroke in 2012. "until he died of a stroke in 2012."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Internet Meme Status
podcast.body: His 1976 Soviet TV performance of "I am very glad as I am finally returning home" went viral around 2010, becoming known as the "Trollolo song." The video was so popular it was sometimes used as a "rick roll." "Around 2010, this performance became a meme and swept the internet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prominent Soviet Singer
podcast.body: Edward Hill, whose anglicized name is used, was a significant figure in the USSR, known as the "symbol of Leningrad" and receiving official government awards. He was a music teacher and toured over 80 countries, indicating a serious musical background. "He was a really big deal at one point with all kinds of official government rewards bestowed upon him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Self-Renaming
podcast.body: Following the viral success of the meme, Hill embraced the phenomenon and started calling himself "Mr. Trollolo." "That afterwards, Hill started calling himself Mr. Trollolo until he died of a stroke in 2012."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unconventional Performance
podcast.body: His choice to perform a song with a wordless, jovial vocalization on national TV suggests a unique artistic sensibility, potentially aligning him with outsider musicians despite his mainstream success. "Is Edward Hill an outsider musician? I don't know, but you've got to have something special if you're going to do something like this, a national TV."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
